lessons.title: Inventory
lessons.summary: Managed hosts and their grouping or connection data.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Inventory selection determines the potential execution scope.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A production play unexpectedly targets a staging group too. Inspect inventory groups and the resolved host pattern before execution.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It is a list of Docker image layers. This is not a sound assumption; managed hosts and their grouping or connection data.

lessons.takeaway: Inventory selection determines the potential execution scope.

lessons.title: Playbooks
lessons.summary: Plays mapping tasks and roles to target hosts.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Task order and conditions affect execution behavior.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A task intended for web servers runs on database hosts. Correct the play's host selection and verify the resolved list.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It is only a database of passwords. This is not a sound assumption; plays mapping tasks and roles to target hosts.

lessons.takeaway: Task order and conditions affect execution behavior.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.summary: Modules often model desired state and support idempotent behavior.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Module documentation defines supported parameters and return values.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A shell task appends the same configuration line on every run. Use an appropriate declarative file or configuration module.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every shell command is automatically idempotent. This is not a sound assumption; modules often model desired state and support idempotent behavior.

lessons.takeaway: Module documentation defines supported parameters and return values.

lessons.title: Idempotence
lessons.summary: Repeated execution can preserve the already-correct desired state.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A no-change run is useful evidence but not a complete correctness proof.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A second identical run still recreates an unchanged configuration file. Inspect task behavior and use state-aware operations.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An idempotent task must execute exactly once forever. This is not a sound assumption; repeated execution can preserve the already-correct desired state.

lessons.takeaway: A no-change run is useful evidence but not a complete correctness proof.

lessons.title: Become
lessons.summary: Privilege escalation for selected operations.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Escalation should be scoped to tasks that need it.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A task needs root only to install one package. Scope privilege escalation and use the package module.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It automatically encrypts all variables. This is not a sound assumption; privilege escalation for selected operations.

lessons.takeaway: Escalation should be scoped to tasks that need it.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.summary: Values can come from multiple sources with precedence rules.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Unexpected values should be traced to their actual source.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A host uses a different port than its role default. Inspect higher-precedence inventory and runtime overrides.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The last alphabetic variable name always wins. This is not a sound assumption; values can come from multiple sources with precedence rules.

lessons.takeaway: Unexpected values should be traced to their actual source.

lessons.title: Facts
lessons.summary: Discover host characteristics for conditional automation.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Facts can become stale if cached beyond relevant changes.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A cached operating-system fact no longer matches a rebuilt host. Refresh relevant facts and inspect cache policy.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Facts are always a live view of every host property. This is not a sound assumption; discover host characteristics for conditional automation.

lessons.takeaway: Facts can become stale if cached beyond relevant changes.

lessons.title: Handlers
lessons.summary: At defined handler execution points after notifying changes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Multiple notifications can coalesce into one handler execution.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Three configuration tasks require one service restart. Notify a shared handler and verify the restart timing.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every handler runs after every task unconditionally. This is not a sound assumption; at defined handler execution points after notifying changes.

lessons.takeaway: Multiple notifications can coalesce into one handler execution.

lessons.title: Check mode
lessons.summary: Support and predictive accuracy depend on the module and task.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A dry run does not prove every runtime side effect is safe.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A task depends on output from a command skipped in check mode. Review check-mode support and test safely in a representative environment.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Check mode guarantees an exact simulation of every shell command. This is not a sound assumption; support and predictive accuracy depend on the module and task.

lessons.takeaway: A dry run does not prove every runtime side effect is safe.

lessons.title: Diff mode
lessons.summary: It can reveal sensitive configuration content.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Secret-bearing tasks may need protected output and no_log.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A template diff shows credentials in CI logs. Suppress sensitive output and review exposure and credential rotation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Diff output can never contain secrets. This is not a sound assumption; it can reveal sensitive configuration content.

lessons.takeaway: Secret-bearing tasks may need protected output and no_log.

lessons.title: Vault
lessons.summary: Encrypted content at rest when properly managed.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Decrypted values can still leak through task output or external systems.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An encrypted secret is printed by a debug task. Remove the disclosure and protect runtime logging.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Vault prevents every runtime secret exposure. This is not a sound assumption; encrypted content at rest when properly managed.

lessons.takeaway: Decrypted values can still leak through task output or external systems.

lessons.title: Templates
lessons.summary: Render configuration from variables and expressions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rendered configuration should be validated before service activation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A rendered web-server configuration has invalid syntax. Validate the candidate configuration before replacing or reloading it.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Templates guarantee valid syntax for every target service. This is not a sound assumption; render configuration from variables and expressions.

lessons.takeaway: Rendered configuration should be validated before service activation.

lessons.title: Roles
lessons.summary: Related tasks defaults handlers and supporting files.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Roles benefit from explicit interfaces and limited assumptions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A shared role requires undocumented variables and breaks callers. Document defaults and required inputs and test representative callers.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A role is necessarily a separate remote user account. This is not a sound assumption; related tasks defaults handlers and supporting files.

lessons.takeaway: Roles benefit from explicit interfaces and limited assumptions.

lessons.title: Collections
lessons.summary: Distribute related modules plugins and roles.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Pinning tested collection versions helps reproducibility.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: CI fails because a module collection is absent on a clean runner. Declare and install versioned collection requirements.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Collections are always included in every ansible-core installation. This is not a sound assumption; distribute related modules plugins and roles.

lessons.takeaway: Pinning tested collection versions helps reproducibility.

lessons.title: FQCNs
lessons.summary: Make the intended module namespace explicit.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Explicit names reduce ambiguity when collections overlap.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two collections provide similarly named modules. Use the intended collection namespace and verify its documentation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A fully qualified name automatically grants more privileges. This is not a sound assumption; make the intended module namespace explicit.

lessons.takeaway: Explicit names reduce ambiguity when collections overlap.

lessons.title: Conditionals
lessons.summary: Whether a task executes for a host based on a condition.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Conditions should use correctly typed and available values.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A task unexpectedly runs because a string value was treated as truthy. Normalize input types and inspect the condition.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It changes inventory membership permanently. This is not a sound assumption; whether a task executes for a host based on a condition.

lessons.takeaway: Conditions should use correctly typed and available values.

lessons.title: Registered results
lessons.summary: A task result for later use in the play.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Result fields depend on the module and execution outcome.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A later task accesses stdout on a skipped result. Guard for skipped or missing result fields.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Register stores a permanent system environment variable. This is not a sound assumption; a task result for later use in the play.

lessons.takeaway: Result fields depend on the module and execution outcome.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.summary: Avoid variable collisions in nested or included tasks.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Loop results often require handling a collection of per-item results.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An included task overwrites the outer item variable. Use loop_control with distinct variable names.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A loop always executes on all hosts serially. This is not a sound assumption; avoid variable collisions in nested or included tasks.

lessons.takeaway: Loop results often require handling a collection of per-item results.

lessons.title: Failure conditions
lessons.summary: The condition under which a task is considered failed.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Exit status and output semantics should guide failure criteria.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A command returns a documented nonzero code for a harmless state. Define an explicit failure condition matching the command contract.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It suppresses all future errors automatically. This is not a sound assumption; the condition under which a task is considered failed.

lessons.takeaway: Exit status and output semantics should guide failure criteria.

lessons.title: Change reporting
lessons.summary: Whether a task reports that it changed state.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Accurate change reporting affects handler notifications.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A read-only diagnostic command triggers a restart handler. Mark the diagnostic as unchanged when appropriate.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It prevents the command from executing. This is not a sound assumption; whether a task reports that it changed state.

lessons.takeaway: Accurate change reporting affects handler notifications.

lessons.title: Serial rollout
lessons.summary: The batch size of hosts processed through the play.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Batch size should reflect availability and failure-domain constraints.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A fleet-wide restart would remove all serving capacity. Use bounded batches with health verification and stop criteria.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It changes the number of CPU cores on each host. This is not a sound assumption; the batch size of hosts processed through the play.

lessons.takeaway: Batch size should reflect availability and failure-domain constraints.

lessons.title: Delegation
lessons.summary: The host on which a task executes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Variable and connection context need care with delegated tasks.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A load-balancer update should run through a control endpoint. Delegate the specific operation and verify credentials and context.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It permanently moves every later task to that host. This is not a sound assumption; the host on which a task executes.

lessons.takeaway: Variable and connection context need care with delegated tasks.

lessons.title: Run once
lessons.summary: Execution can occur once per batch rather than once for the whole inventory.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Global singleton actions need explicit design under batching.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A migration unexpectedly repeats during a serial rollout. Review batch semantics and implement a deliberate singleton migration step.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Run_once always means once across every possible play execution. This is not a sound assumption; execution can occur once per batch rather than once for the whole inventory.

lessons.takeaway: Global singleton actions need explicit design under batching.

lessons.title: Blocks and rescue
lessons.summary: Handle qualifying task failures with recovery steps.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Recovery logic must still account for partial side effects.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A deployment task fails after writing part of its configuration. Use explicit recovery and verify the resulting host state.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Rescue automatically rolls back every previous change. This is not a sound assumption; handle qualifying task failures with recovery steps.

lessons.takeaway: Recovery logic must still account for partial side effects.

lessons.title: Async tasks
lessons.summary: Long-running tasks without holding a normal synchronous wait.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Polling and completion handling must match operational needs.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A long maintenance task exceeds the default connection wait. Use bounded async execution and track the final result.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Async automatically guarantees successful completion. This is not a sound assumption; long-running tasks without holding a normal synchronous wait.

lessons.takeaway: Polling and completion handling must match operational needs.

lessons.title: Tags
lessons.summary: Required prerequisite tasks may be skipped.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Tagged execution needs testing as its own supported path.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Running only a deployment tag skips required configuration setup. Test the selected path and encode needed prerequisites deliberately.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Tags always resolve every prerequisite automatically. This is not a sound assumption; required prerequisite tasks may be skipped.

lessons.takeaway: Tagged execution needs testing as its own supported path.

lessons.title: Dynamic inventory
lessons.summary: Discover hosts from an external authoritative source.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Discovery filters and credentials determine scope.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A cloud inventory plugin includes hosts from an unintended environment. Narrow discovery filters and inspect the generated inventory.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Dynamic inventory can never become stale. This is not a sound assumption; discover hosts from an external authoritative source.

lessons.takeaway: Discovery filters and credentials determine scope.

lessons.title: Concurrency
lessons.summary: Overload of targets controllers or shared dependencies.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Concurrency should match workload and service capacity.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A configuration run overloads a shared package repository. Bound concurrency and stage work based on dependency capacity.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: More forks always reduces risk. This is not a sound assumption; overload of targets controllers or shared dependencies.

lessons.takeaway: Concurrency should match workload and service capacity.

lessons.title: Secret logging
lessons.summary: Sensitive task data from normal Ansible output.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It does not prevent a command from leaking secrets into external files or services.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A task hides output but writes a password into a world-readable file. Fix file handling and permissions in addition to suppressing logs.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: No_log encrypts every remote file created by a task. This is not a sound assumption; sensitive task data from normal Ansible output.

lessons.takeaway: It does not prevent a command from leaking secrets into external files or services.

lessons.title: Automation validation
lessons.summary: Representative execution and checks of the resulting system behavior.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Syntax checks cannot prove target permissions or service readiness.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A play passes lint but fails during a live service reload. Test in a representative environment with explicit postconditions.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Syntax success guarantees the play is safe for production. This is not a sound assumption; representative execution and checks of the resulting system behavior.

lessons.takeaway: Syntax checks cannot prove target permissions or service readiness.
